full_judgment: 6. Mr. Abul Khair submits that the surveyor having had, reported that the land settled with the plaintiff measuring .10 decimals out of .73 decimals was no longer a gopath and drain and was turned into an agricultural land by cultivating the same by the petitioner and his predecessor who had been in possession of the same and the same not being required by the public as pathway, the lease was granted rightly in favour of the petitioner who satisfied the requirement of Section 76 of State Acquisition & Tenancy Act, 1950. Secondly, placing reliance on Rule 105 of the Government Estate Mannual, he submits that the lower appellate Court erred in holding that upon an application of a third party, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) was competent to cancel the lease as an appellate authority.
